_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Mongolia covering Xiongnu confederation, Turks/Uyghur khaganates, Khitan Liao, Genghis Khan's Mongol Empire (1206, largest contiguous empire), Yuan Dynasty, Northern Yuan, Manchu Qing conquest, Bogd Khanate (1911 independence), Outer Mongolia autonomy, Soviet-backed Mongolian People's Republic (1924, second communist state), 1990 democratic revolution, market economy transition, mining boom, and balancing China-Russia via 'third neighbour' policy.

religion.note: Tibetan Buddhism suppressed under communism; revival post-1990; Gandantegchinlen Monastery; Dalai Lama ties; Kazakhs are Muslim; shamanic/Tengriist traditions persist; communist era left large non-religious population

ethnic_groups.name: Khalkha Mongol
ethnic_groups.notes: Dominant group; standard Mongolian based on Khalkha dialect; nomadic pastoralist traditions (though urbanising); Cyrillic script since 1941; politically dominant

ethnic_groups.name: Kazakh
ethnic_groups.notes: Bayan-Ölgii province; Muslim; Turkic language; eagle hunting; autonomous cultural region; some emigration to Kazakhstan

ethnic_groups.name: Dorvod
ethnic_groups.notes: Oirat subgroup; western Mongolia; distinct dialect

ethnic_groups.name: Buryat
ethnic_groups.notes: Northern Mongolia; cross-border with Russia (Buryatia); Buddhist; some Russian cultural influence

ethnic_groups.name: Zakhchin, Dariganga, Uriankhai, other Mongolic
ethnic_groups.notes: Various Mongol tribes; Oirat and Khalkha subgroups; reindeer-herding Tsaatan (Dukha) in far north

ethnic_groups.name: Chinese, Russian, Tuvan, Other
ethnic_groups.notes: Small Chinese and Russian minorities; Tuvan in far west; communist-era Russians mostly left

independence.from: Qing China (1911), then Mongolia People's Republic declared 1924; independence recognised by China only 1945

country_profile.notes_unique: World's most sparsely populated sovereign country (~2 people/km²); landlocked between China and Russia; Genghis Khan legacy central to national identity; Oyu Tolgoi (massive copper/gold mine); nomadic pastoralism (~30% nomadic); coldest capital city globally; Gobi Desert; wild horses (Przewalski); throat singing (khöömei); 'third neighbour' policy balances China-Russia via US/Japan/EU ties

trade.notes: China 90%+ of exports (extreme dependency); Oyu Tolgoi copper (Rio Tinto); coal to China via Gashuunsukhait; cashmere 2nd globally; landlocked transit costs high.

infrastructure.notes: Vast distances, minimal paved roads; Trans-Mongolian Railway (Ulaanbaatar-Russia/China); new Chinggis Khaan airport (2021); power imports from Russia; ger district electricity challenges.

governance_indices.notes: Post-1990 democratic transition largely successful; MPP dominant party; competitive elections; mining corruption scandals; civil society relatively active; press freedom declining.

country_profile.national_anthem: Mongol Ulsyn Toriin Duulal (National Anthem of Mongolia)

geography.terrain: Vast semi-arid steppe; mountainous west and north (Altai, Khangai); Gobi Desert south; grasslands central
geography.notes: World's most sparsely populated sovereign nation (2/km²); landlocked between Russia and China; Genghis Khan homeland; nomadic herding heritage; Gobi rich in dinosaur fossils.

economy_extended.notes: Mining-dominated (Oyu Tolgoi copper-gold, Tavan Tolgoi coal); 'resource curse' concerns; Chinggis Bond (2012) landmark; third-neighbor policy (US, Japan, EU); Dutch disease risk.

health.notes: Highest liver cancer rate globally (hepatitis B/C); ger district ger areas lack sanitation; Ulaanbaatar air pollution health crisis (winter); nomad healthcare access challenging.

food_agriculture.notes: Pastoral nomadism with 70M+ livestock; cashmere goats 2nd globally; dzud (severe winter) kills millions of animals periodically; meat/dairy staple diet; limited arable farming.

security_stability.notes: Peaceful democracy; 'third neighbor' policy balancing Russia-China; active UN peacekeeper; nuclear-weapon-free zone; no major conflicts since 1990 transition.

environment_climate.notes: Ulaanbaatar among world's most polluted capitals (winter ger district coal burning); desertification advancing; dzud climate events; snow leopard habitat; Gobi ecosystem fragile.

demographics_extended.notes: Ethnically homogeneous (Khalkha Mongol 85%+); Kazakh minority (3.5%) in west; rapid urbanization (45% in Ulaanbaatar); nomadic population declining; high female education rates.

comparative_rankings._note: Country position relative to continent and global.
comparative_rankings.notes: Most sparsely populated country; landlocked between Russia and China; mining-dependent economy; democratic oasis in region.

cultural_heritage.national_sport: Three manly games: wrestling, horse racing, archery
world_heritage_sites: Petroglyphic Complexes of the Mongolian Altai
Deer Stone Monuments and Related Bronze Age Sites
cultural_heritage.media_landscape: UB Post, Mongol Messenger (English); MNB, Eagle TV; relatively free press by regional standards.
cultural_heritage.notes: Genghis Khan (largest contiguous land empire); nomadic pastoral tradition; ger (yurt) living; Buddhist (Gelug) revival; throat singing world-renowned.

energy.notes: Coal-dependent; Tavan Tolgoi (world's largest untapped coking coal deposit); wind/solar potential in Gobi; imports electricity from Russia; Gobi wind farms expanding.

human_rights_gender.lgbtq_legal_status: Legal since 2002; discrimination ban in Criminal Code (2024 reform)
human_rights_gender.notes: Rare democracy in Central/East Asia region; press freedom; mining corruption concerns; domestic violence law (2016); herder displacement.

legal_system.notes: Constitutional Court; Supreme Court; democratic constitution since 1992; judicial reform ongoing; mining law critical; nomadic grazing land rights.

tourism.notes: Adventure and nomadic tourism; ger camps; horseback trekking; Gobi expeditions; limited infrastructure but growing.

transport.notes: Trans-Mongolian Railway (Moscow–Beijing); landlocked; vast unpaved road network; new Chinggis Khaan Airport (2021); MIAT Mongolian Airlines.

910.name: Xiongnu Empire
910.description: The first great nomadic empire of the Mongolian steppe, the Xiongnu confederation that rivaled Han China, built the template for steppe empires, and may be ancestral to the European Huns.
